the excess of sulphate (from the industrial effluent), in the upper layers of the sediments, favoured the abundant Fe(III) oxides, which appear to act as a barrier limiting mercury escape to the water column.

the high content of sulphate in the pore waters of Tagus estuary, due to the industrial input, may explain the formation of abundant Fe-oxhydroxides in the upper layers of sediments, which act as a barrier limiting mercury release to the water column.
